correctness.rationale: For r>=2, all n_i>=1, N=sum n_i>=2, unit cross edges, and uniform vertex masses, the squared operator norm of T_G is maximum centered variance. Anchoring at one vertex makes the feasible Lipschitz ball compact, and variance is strictly convex on that anchored affine space, so every maximizer must be a polytope vertex. At a vertex tight-edge incidence rank N-1 forces a spanning tight tree; summing +/-1 along its edges proves integrality. Since complete multipartite graph diameter is <=2, normalized extremal values are binary {0,1} or {-1,0,1}. The latter requires both signs within a single part, every outside vertex at zero, and no same-part zeros (they would be isolated in the tight-edge graph). Exact variance numerator equals t(N-t) for binary with t ones, or N*a-(2k-a)^2 for a +/-1 part with k positive signs. The former maximizes at floor(N²/4), the latter at N*m-(m mod2), monotone in a. All maximizing equality classes follow from these sharp cases. Singleton m=1 has no three-level type, including harmless N=2,3 algebraic ties. Writing N=4q+r and evaluating m=q and q+1 in residues r=0,1,2,3 establishes baseline iff m<=floor(N/4) for N>=4, and true coexistence exactly when N divisible by 8 and m=N/4. I independently enumerated all 58 unordered connected multipartite profiles N=2..8, 13800 feasible anchored integer assignments, all 968 maximizers and the classification; repeated exact threshold arithmetic for every N=4..1500 and m<N. Rebuilt both source and checks Git trees from all seven file and directory SHA identities: root ab29f40ac8925d33336695e4808476daa75792ac. These finite checks corroborate but do not replace the all-N proof.
residual_risks: Restricted to real-valued scalar maps, uniform mass, unweighted simple connected complete multipartite graphs with >=2 parts. The Hilbert-valued or nonuniform analogue is not proved.
Finite enumeration and exact arithmetic over a bounded N range are only corroboration; the general proof rests on strict convexity, incidence-rank and four-residue identities.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing facet classification is geometrically stronger but does not numerically imply a sharp quadratic maximum without actually comparing the faces. The missing-edge-budget theorem gives only an adversarial envelope: the complete multipartite complement is a disjoint union of cliques, and the degree envelope max{floor(N²/4),2N(m-1)} is not the claimed exact Nm-(m mod 2). The two-distance bipartite formula covers r=2 only and internally describes the all-part endpoint as prior; same-day indexing is insufficient for publication ordering. The Hilbert-valued theorem covers different targets and even has a different constant.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Lipschitz-to-L2 norm squared equals graph spread by the elementary identity ||f-Ef||_2²=Var(f). The same domain is the anchored dual unit ball of the graph symmetric-edge polytope. Proposition 3.5 classifies its vertices but does not state the largest-part variance optimization or quarter-part selection. The bipartite published endpoint agrees when r=2 but not arbitrary r and does not dominate the all-part statement.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: the exact uniform scalar spread, all maximizing assignments, and quarter-size plateau for arbitrary complete multipartite graphs were not found as a pre-existing full theorem in the inspected primary literature or nearby published findings. The original source itself occurs in the Resultary index and is not counted as independent prior coverage. Strong 2018 facet results already classify potential shapes; novelty is the explicit centered quadratic optimization, integer parity boundary, and equality selection, not new polytope vertices. A separate published two-distance bipartite theorem covers the two-part t=2 special case while explicitly crediting an earlier multipartite scalar endpoint; its dated same-day occurrence cannot prove earlier priority for the all-part claim.

The scalar t=2 bipartite subfamily is present as a published 2026-11-08 theorem that credits a previously published multipartite scalar endpoint; precise within-day order is not established by dates alone.

value.rationale: Graph spread is a natural sharp scalar Lipschitz-to-centered-L2 concentration/embedding constant. Within an infinite, symmetric but parametrically nontrivial family the result gives an exact all-size operator norm, all norming functions and an exact quarter-largest-part stability plateau under extensive edge deletion. The parity-only coexistence at N divisible by 8 and balanced K_{s,s,s,s} exhibiting unchanged spread after deletion of asymptotically one quarter of clique edges are mathematically motivated non-strictness/phase phenomena. Although the candidate facet geometries are known, their exact centered quadratic optimization and global transition are not merely renaming the known facet count. The proof is elementary once the prior structural theorem is recognized, and its scope/value are stated accordingly.
residual_risks: The work is a sharp specialized optimization on known facet types, not a new general Lipschitz-free space theorem.
The quarter threshold is for uniform scalar L2 variance only, not necessarily for broader concentration or Hilbert-valued constants.
